scope: Single-host serial installed CommonJS package experiment, 5000 paragraphs / 6 cycles / checkpoint every 3 cycles; baseline/candidate then candidate/baseline. Semantic assertions and acceptance limits remain unchanged. No browser/GitLab performance comparison or production-readiness claim. Memory observations are not a universal leak threshold.
candidate: An internal WeakSet certified only flat frozen attribute snapshots produced by freezeAttributes. External objects, host instances, nested values, active ancestor guards and all attribute/node validators remained on their existing paths. Weak-key membership and registration did not improve the measured workload.
retainedRegressions: Active ancestors on flat/nested snapshots; dynamic foreign frozen accessors; proxy inspection after host revocation; rejection of symbols, bigint and functions by deep immutability checks. Existing retained-store tests rerun live attribute/whole-node validators and mutable host defaults.
wireSizeNote: Portable content digests and update/duplicate counts match. Encoded traffic is 102345-102356 bytes, not byte-identical. Restored Y.Doc clients get fresh client IDs and each adapter uses retainedIdentityAllocator on a random UUID; these identifiers and their compact lengths vary. Actual per-run bytes and checkpoint client IDs are retained; no universal wire-size regression/improvement claim is made.
